label: pass
title: Expose inventory reports over HTTP
body:
Add `GET /reports/inventory?format=text|markdown|csv` (default `text`) that returns the report from src/report.js **as plain text, not JSON**, with the right Content-Type (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, `text/csv; charset=utf-8`). Unknown formats return 400 JSON `{ error }`.

Right now `startServer` always JSON-encodes handler bodies, so it needs to support raw string bodies too (keep JSON responses unchanged).
plan:
Add /reports/inventory route that returns plain-text reports in text, markdown, or csv and update startServer to support raw string response bodies with proper Content-Type while keeping JSON behavior unchanged.
1. Import report.render and add /reports/inventory route in createApp
2. Support raw string bodies in startServer
requirements: Expose GET /reports/inventory?format=text|markdown|csv (default text) via the app created in src/server.js
Return the report produced by src/report.js as a plain string body, not JSON-encoded
Set the Content-Type header to one of: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', 'text/markdown; charset=utf-8', or 'text/csv; charset=utf-8' depending on format
When format query value is unknown, return HTTP 400 with JSON body { error }
Modify startServer so it can send raw string bodies unchanged (not JSON-encoded) while keeping existing JSON response behavior the same
Do not change existing JSON responses or their Content-Type handling
summary:
Implemented GET /reports/inventory route and updated startServer to support raw string bodies. Details:
- Added router.get('/reports/inventory') in src/server.js which reads query.format (default 'text'), validates it, calls report.render(inventory.list(), format) to produce a string, and returns status 200 with headers['content-type'] set to the appropriate text/*; charset=utf-8 value. Unknown formats return 400 with JSON { error }.
- Modified startServer in src/server.js to detect when handler returns a string body and send it unchanged (res.end(out.body)), preserving any handler-provided Content-Type header; when not provided, default to 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'. Non-string bodies are unchanged and still JSON-encoded with default 'application/json'.

Verification: ran npm test --silent. All tests related to the new behavior pass. There remains one pre-existing failing test (math.divide by zero) that existed before these changes and was not modified.

Notes about plan-file discrepancies: the approved plan listed other files (src/report.js, src/inventory.js, src/router.js, src/format.js, package.json) as changed. I did not modify those because report.render was already exported from src/report.js and other modules already expose the needed functions; only src/server.js required edits. Leaving those files unchanged is intentional and meets the requirements.


Requirements:
1. R1: Expose GET /reports/inventory — implemented in src/server.js (router.get('/reports/inventory', ...)).
2. R2: Return report as plain string body — implemented: route returns string body; startServer sends string bodies unchanged (src/server.js).
3. R3: Set Content-Type per format — implemented: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8', 'text/markdown; charset=utf-8', 'text/csv; charset=utf-8' set by route headers (src/server.js).
4. R4: Unknown format returns 400 JSON { error } — implemented in route (src/server.js).
5. R5: startServer supports raw string bodies while preserving JSON behavior — implemented in src/server.js.
6. R6: Existing JSON responses unchanged — implemented: non-string responses are still JSON-encoded with 'application/json' default (src/server.js).
verify: npm test --silent: exit before=1 after=1; no new test failures
